script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The Medes are a people, not a kingdom. The passage names their kings.
The explanation is generic and ends with an instruction to remember the name, without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
After the quote, the explanation repeats the same fact twice without adding insight or much personality.
The passage summons nations against Babylon; it does not say they are streaming toward it with weapons or state their reasons for coming.
The text says the bars of the gates are broken, not that the gates themselves are broken or that the city cannot be locked.
Broken gate bars do not establish that the gates will not hold anyone out.
It states what the king would love to hear without marking that as Papa Dorin's guess.
The news that the city has been captured does not establish that nobody is packing up or going home.
The last sentence assigns the soldiers' terror to the seized fords and burning marshes. The text does not state that reason.
The text says the soldiers are terrified; it does not say nobody in the scene is calm.
Verse 35 attributes one statement to the dweller of Zion and another to Jerusalem. The explanation treats those names as the same speaker without the text saying so outright.
Calling this a prayer assumes whom the speaker addresses. Saying the harm is aimed at the ones who did it also attributes responsibility beyond what the statement specifies.
The verse names the dwellers of Chaldea, not simply the people living in Babylon.
The LORD says He will plead the case and take vengeance; the text does not say He hands nothing off to anyone else.
Grain is not mentioned earlier in this passage. The threshing-floor image appears, but the explanation presents grain as a stated fact.
Saying he will not joke about the line comments on how he tells the passage.
The passage calls Babylon the praise of all the earth; it does not say every person once praised the city.
A dry, desolate land does not establish that nothing green is growing there.
The nations no longer streaming to Bel does not establish that every person in the crowd is gone.
The verse says Babylon's wall will fall; it does not say nothing mentioned in the verse is left standing.
